newsitem.title: USA: U.S. propane lifted by crude's rebound.
newsitem.headline: U.S. propane lifted by crude's rebound.

text.p: U.S. spot prices of propane, an important liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), bounced back up slightly in quiet late trade on Monday amid a rebound in NYMEX crude oil futures, players said.
Propane prices and other LPGs in the U.S. fell this morning following a fall in NYMEX March crude oil amid weak demand for refined products.
In late trade, Conway, Kansas, anytime propane was assessed between 38.00 cents and 38.75 cents, one penny above midday levels, but still a penny down from Friday.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, selled edged up a quarter to 37.00 cents, with buyers still at 36.50 cents.
"Crude's driving down propane. Other than that there is not much news," said one Houston broker.
The butane markets were slightly higher to steady in thin trade.
NYMEX March crude oil ended up 23 cents at $22.46 a barrel.
